english.title: Cause or permit false statement of candidates name or address to be furnished to returning officer at election
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were guilty of a corrupt practice in that you caused or permitted a statement of the

(A)_[name]_
(B)_[home address]_
(C)_[name and home address]_

of a candidate at a

(D)_[parliamentary]_
(E)_[local government]_

election to be included in a document delivered or furnished to a returning officer for use in connection with that election knowing the statement to be false in a particular, namely **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF FALSE STATEMENT..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 65A(1)(a) and 168 of the Representation of the People Act 1983.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
in the case of any relevant election
causes or permits to be included in a document delivered or otherwise furnished to a returning officer
for use in connection with the election
a statement of the name or home address of a candidate at the election which he knows to be false in any particular

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See Section 65A(2) for the definition of a relevant election as it applies to this offence
(ii) This offence has been inserted by paragraph 5 of Schedule 6 to the Representation of the People Act 2000

other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
